steps.text: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Stir in popcorn kernels and sugar.
Cover and shake the pot constantly to prevent sugar from burning. When popping has slowed to once every 2 to 3 seconds, remove the pot from the heat and shake for a few minutes until popping stops.
Pour popcorn into a large bowl and allow to cool, stirring occasionally to break up large clumps.

raw_recipe.headline: Kettle Corn
raw_recipe.description: This kettle corn recipe is made on the stovetop with just three ingredients and tastes deliciously old-fashioned and straight from the county fair.

review.reviewBody: Cheap, quick, and easy! I put oil and three kernels in the pot, when all three kernels pop I add the sugar and stir it around well, then I add the rest of the popcorn kernels and put the lid on. Then I alternate shaking the pot for three seconds with letting it sit on the burner for three seconds until I hear the popping begin to slow down, then I take off the lid and sprinkle some salt in, replace the lid, give it another shake and pour it out into a bowl. Haven't had a batch burn yet with the "3-second shake and sit" technique. ;-)

I don't have one of those neat hand-crank popcorn-making-thingys. I have absolutely zero experience making popcorn on the stove. What I do have is a pot that I normally use for chili and pasta, a fondness for kettle corn, and a heck of a of a nerve on me. Here's what I did, mistakes and all: I did the 3-kernel test, and then added the sugar and the popcorn at the same time. (I'm not going to call that a mistake, but I think next time I'll add the sugar, let it melt, and then add the popcorn - the way I did it this afternoon, the popcorn started to pop before the sugar was melted.) I used canola oil and thought it was fine. I added 1 tsp of salt plus a pinch or two to the sugar; next time I might stick to just 1 tsp, as I found some pieces to be a little salty. I did the three-seconds-on-the-heat/three-seconds-off-the-heat thing, shaking the entire time, and I probably pulled it a little early because I'd rather have a few unpopped kernels than burned sugar and popcorn. The end result was very, very tasty. Some of the pieces carmelized quite a bit, others didn't; I preferred the ones that didn't, but that didn't stop me from eating the entire batch by myself. Cleanup was no problem; the cooled sugar melted right off again with hot water. Thanks for the great recipe! Edit: Later, I tried letting the sugar melt before adding the popcorn. I thought the sugar carmelized too much - it tasted burned instead of sweet. I'll add them at the same time from now on.

Wow! This became a really fast hit in my family. After making it a few times, though, I do have some suggestions. The last time I made it was the best. Instead of using oil, I melted about 1/4 cup of butter flavored shortening. It made the kernels pop much faster lighter, and had a hint of a buttery taste. Very nice. I also, added a few drops of decorator's icing coloring to the melted shortening and sugar mixture. When the popcorn pops, it explodes into a really beautiful color.

You can even mix two colors together[only two batches of popcorn is needed for that;)]

I adjusted my recipe for a single eater, so about 1-2tbsp of oil, 3tbsp of kernels, and 1 tbsp of sugar in the pot. I then dusted with a salt and sugar mix as it cooled. I have an electric coil stove, so to avoid the screeching, I let the pot sit for 10-15 seconds, then lifted and shook. If you have never made stovetop popcorn before, I would recommend practicing without sugar first to get the technique down, then make this recipe.

Absolutely delicious. Followed the directions for my whirly pop stovetop popper. Added oil, plus a few kernels and heated. When they started to pop, added the rest of the corn and the sugar. Shook and stirred immediately and continuously until popping ceased. I did add a little fine popcorn salt as suggested. Half a recipe makes a huge snack portion for me alone. Never have to pay for a fair or food truck version again!!

I love this recipe and have made it a dozen or more times, trying to get the best results. I do the following to get the most kernels popped and prevent scorching: have all ingredients measured out into separate containers before starting, stir 1/2 tsp salt into sugar, add oil and 3 kernels to nonstick pot over Medium heat and cover with lid, remove kernels once popped and stir in rest of kernels, leave off heat but covered with lid for about 30 seconds to allow all kernels to come to the same temp, return to heat and sprinkle white sugar on top of kernels (without stirring), cook for 5 seconds then lift from heat and shake vigorously for 5 seconds, repeat heat and shake sequence until popping slows, pour immediately into a large bowl and break up clumps as it cools. This is a perfect recipe... cheap, simple and delicious.

This is simply the BEST kettle corn recipe. So simple, easy, fast, and super delicious. I took KRYSTENL's advice, by adding three kernels to the oil at the beginning and when they pop it's time to add all the popcorn and sugar, then 3 secs on the burner, 3 secs off it shaking the pot, over and over again until the popping slows down. No burning at all! I also added a tablespoon each of butter and coconut oil to the oil (I used sunflower oil) at the very beginning for a little extra flavor! So good! Oh and also I salted the popcorn when it was done popping and I had poured it into a large bowl. A must-try recipe and one that I will make again and again.
Followed the 3-second on/off heat shaking when off to keep from burning. Used enuf oil to cover bottom of SS 2 qt pan… about 3 T. Stir in sugar before adding rest of kernels once the first 3 pop.

This recipe is so good to have in the snack arsenal. I have used it as much for technique in popping corn as well as for the sweet/salty no butter goodness. I have adjusted the recipe to my taste. I use only enough oil to cover the bottom of the pot, once the 3 kernels pop, I add only enough pop corn to cover the bottom of the pot in a single layer, then I sprinkle about 2 or 3 Tbsps of sugar over the corn. I let it heat up a few seconds and start shaking the pot. I also control the heat better by removing the pot from the direct heat occasionally to keep it from possibly burning and I lift the lid up slightly to release some of the moisture so it pops fluffier. I salt the corn as I put it into the bowl a little at a time. I love it because it doesn't need additional butter so it remains crisp and there's no worry about greasy hands !
I used sugar in the raw and coconut oil... also used the 3 kernel method, used a wok with a lid and shook every 15-20 seconds. Have made twice and it was a big hit both times.

I love doing this. As others, I wait for a couple Kernels to pop, I add the sugar, and stir, then add the kernels. It is super easy and rarely burns with the Whirley-Pop to stir the mixture while popping. I also put fine salt on as soon as it goes into the bowl. It's wonderful, and I've been doing it for about 20 yrs.

The sugar burned to the bottom of the pan despite vigourous shaking to prevent it from doing so. I don't know where I went wrong as my results were a fail. I tried this twice with different pans. It took a lot of cleaning to get the burnt sugar off the bottom of the stainless steel pan. No thank you. Not worth a third try to see if it's the recipe or me.

After reading all the problems with burning, I made a little bowl of sugar on the side , & a 1/2 cup butter melted. I popped the corn, then immediately poured on the sugar & mixed . The popcorn was so hot the sugar melted onto it. Then I put a little salt & poured the hot butter over it, & mixed again. It was delicious. I made it again, only this time I put a pinch of cayenne pepper into the butter. Wow, great flavor.

Put oil in, two kernels. When both popped, I put the rest of the kernels in and the sugar, slammed the lid on, and shook the pot like it owed me money. Took it off the heat just before it seemed done, slammed the corn into a different bowl and tossed with salt. 10/10. Tastes just slightly less good than the farmer’s market kettle corn. Would recommend wearing long sleeves and glasses for safety in case a kernel or oil drop flies out.
Loved it....JUST LOVED IT!!!!
It’s very yummy

Not bad, not bad at all. I thought the sugar acted weird though, when I added it to the oil. And then the popcorn. But it did work well in the end. My first batch, I was worried about over-cooking the sugar, and ended up not popping all the corn. The second batch, I was less worried and more of the kernels popped. Pour into a bowl, add salt, and yeah. Pretty darn good. Next time, I'll try the brown sugar.
A clear lid is really helpful to be able to swirl the kernels vigorously and see when they are popped to the point that they can no longer move very much.
it was pretty good! needs improvement in recipe though--> need to add when you put in kernels in sugar plus to put in sugar

I’ve made a lot of traditional popcorn, so I was more confident than most making it. Much messier, having to shake the pan more vigorously, but not too bad. You may want to have pants on to not get hot oil on you. I added (don’t judge haha) a stick of melted butter, authentic maple syrup (infused with a cinnamon stick), and salt I poured on the popcorn right before serving. I even took 2 tablespoons of the butter stick and threw it in right before the kernels started popping. In the end… Delicious!
